artists.biography:
Black Label Society is a heavy metal band from Los Angeles, California formed by Zakk Wylde. The band has, thus far, released nine studio albums, one live album, two compilation albums, one EP, and three video albums.
In the early 1990s, Wylde had formed his own solo band Pride & Glory, playing a mixture of bluesy southern rock with heavy metal. However, they disbanded in December 1994 after having released only one album. Wylde subsequently recorded an acoustic solo album, Book of Shadows (released 1996). In May 1998, after limited commercial success with Book of Shadows, Wylde and drummer Phil Ondich recorded what became Black Label Society's debut album Sonic Brew. It was decided, rather than the album being another solo album for Wylde, that they would form a long term band. It was known from the start that Nick Catanese would be retained as the second guitarist in the band (Catanese previously toured as rhythm guitarist for the Book Of Shadows tour). John DeServio, who previously worked with Wylde as a temporary replacement in Pride & Glory, joined as the band's bassist for the album's tour.

perplexity.description:
Unblackened" is a live acoustic album by Black Label Society, released on September 24, 2013, through E1 Music. Recorded at Club Nokia in Los Angeles in March 2013, the album showcases the band in a stripped-down, mostly acoustic setting, diverging from their typical heavy metal and southern rock sound. The double-disc set features live renditions of classic Black Label Society tracks alongside six newly recorded studio songs, including re-recordings of earlier material. The presence of keyboards and piano, notably by Derek Sherinian, adds a melodic depth that balances the acoustic heaviness, highlighting Zakk Wylde's versatility as both a guitarist and vocalist.

Positioned uniquely within Black Label Society's discography, "Unblackened" offers a fresh perspective on their music, emphasizing atmosphere and musicianship over raw power. It stands out as an authentic live recording that captures the band's dynamic performance in an intimate setting. Critically, the album was well received for its reinterpretations of familiar songs and the quality of the acoustic arrangements, with particular praise for tracks like "House of Doom" and the cover of "Ain't No Sunshine When She's Gone." The release was accompanied by a deluxe edition including a DVD of the show and collectible items, reflecting its significance to fans.
